column1: While these two historical examples are consistent with the permanent-income hypothesis, it is hard to draw firm inferences from them. At any moment in time, there are many macroeconomic influences on consumer spending, including the overall confidence that consumers have in their own economic prospects. It is hard to disentangle the effects of tax policy from the effects of other events occurring at the same time. Fortunately, some recent research has reached more reliable conclusions, as discussed in the next Case Study. n
